example_label: Example data. Fictional agency and AI system. Not a real assessment.

answers.q2_agency: Maryland Office of Family Subsidy Standards (fictional)
answers.q5_changes: State staff set the ranking weights. No vendor and no outside model.
answers.q6_description: The desk scores a child-care subsidy file from application data and household size, then orders the queue. It runs in the state data center. A benefits supervisor decides each award. Fictional system.
answers.q7_purpose: Today supervisors sort paper files by arrival date. The desk proposes an order so older complete files and flagged files surface first. Staff still decide every award. Fictional purpose.
answers.q8_how: It orders subsidy files. A supervisor decides each award.
answers.q14_sources: State child-care subsidy applications held by the subsidy review unit.
answers.q20_harm: A wrong score could move a complete file behind others, so a family waits longer for a child-care subsidy. The cost falls on the applicant. Staff can still change the order.
